steps.title: The five principles of training are known as SPORT
steps.body: S pecificity, P rogressive Overload, O verload, R eversibility, T edium

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Training should be matched to the needs of the sport and the individual. The training must be relevant to the activities and components of fitness required by the performer's sport.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Gradually increasing the demands of training over time so the body continues to adapt and improve. If training stays the same, the body will plateau and no further improvements will occur.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Making the body work harder than normal to cause adaptation. The body must be stressed beyond its current capability for training adaptations to occur.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the principle of specificity and give a sporting example. | What is progressive overload and why is it necessary? | Explain the principle of reversibility and how it affects an injured athlete.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Specificity means training should be matched to the needs of the sport and the individual. Training must focus on the specific fitness components and movements required. Example: a sprinter should tra | Progressive overload means gradually increasing the demands of training over time so the body continues to adapt. It is necessary because if training remains the same, the body adapts to the stimulus  | Reversibility means training adaptations are lost when training stops or is significantly reduced ("use it or lose it"). An injured athlete who cannot train will lose fitness: cardiovascular endurance

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know both SPORT and FITT acronyms inside-out - both are frequently tested Always give a sporting example when explaining a principle Reversibility = "use it or lose it" - this memorable phrase often earns marks FITT is specifically about HOW to increase progressive overload Be ready to apply SPORT and FITT to design a training programme for a specific sport Remember: progressive overload is GRADUAL - don't increase too much too quickly
